answer:
The father of Andreas Vesalius, who is widely regarded as the founder of modern human anatomy, was **Anders van Wesel** (sometimes also written as Andries van Wesel). 

Vesalius was born in Brussels in 1514 as Andries van Wesel, and he later Latinized his name to Andreas Vesalius. His father Anders van Wesel worked as an apothecary to Charles V, Holy Roman Emperor, which may have provided some educational opportunities for young Andreas that would later enable him to revolutionize anatomical studies with his groundbreaking work "De Humani Corporis Fabrica."
